claim: Fiber photometry has become a popular technique to measure neural activity in vivo.
source: Fiber photometry has become a popular technique to measure neural activity in vivo, but common analysis strategies can reduce the detection of effects because they condense within-trial signals into summary measures, and discard trial-level information by averaging across-trials.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a general characterization of the field.

claim: Common fiber photometry analysis strategies condense within-trial signals into summary measures.
source: Fiber photometry has become a popular technique to measure neural activity in vivo, but common analysis strategies can reduce the detection of effects because they condense within-trial signals into summary measures, and discard trial-level information by averaging across-trials.
evidence: This is stated as a characterization of existing methods in the abstract.

claim: Common fiber photometry analysis strategies discard trial-level information by averaging across-trials.
source: Fiber photometry has become a popular technique to measure neural activity in vivo, but common analysis strategies can reduce the detection of effects because they condense within-trial signals into summary measures, and discard trial-level information by averaging across-trials.
evidence: This is stated as a characterization of existing methods in the abstract.

claim: Common fiber photometry analysis strategies can reduce the detection of effects.
source: Fiber photometry has become a popular technique to measure neural activity in vivo, but common analysis strategies can reduce the detection of effects because they condense within-trial signals into summary measures, and discard trial-level information by averaging across-trials.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of existing methods in the abstract.

claim: The proposed FLMM framework enables hypothesis testing of variable effects at every trial time-point.
source: We propose a novel photometry statistical framework based on functional linear mixed modeling, which enables hypothesis testing of variable effects at every trial time-point, and uses trial-level signals without averaging.
evidence: This is stated as a capability of the proposed method in the abstract.

claim: The proposed FLMM framework uses trial-level signals without averaging.
source: We propose a novel photometry statistical framework based on functional linear mixed modeling, which enables hypothesis testing of variable effects at every trial time-point, and uses trial-level signals without averaging.
evidence: This is stated as a capability of the proposed method in the abstract.

claim: The FLMM framework makes it possible to compare the timing and magnitude of signals across conditions while accounting for between-animal differences.
source: This makes it possible to compare the timing and magnitude of signals across conditions while accounting for between-animal differences.
evidence: This is stated as a capability of the proposed method in the abstract.

claim: The FLMM framework produces a series of plots that illustrate covariate effect estimates and statistical significance at each trial time-point.
source: Our framework produces a series of plots that illustrate covariate effect estimates and statistical significance at each trial time-point.
evidence: This is stated as an output of the proposed method in the abstract.

claim: The FLMM methodology yields joint 95% confidence intervals that account for inspecting effects across the entire trial.
source: By exploiting signal autocorrelation, our methodology yields joint 95% confidence intervals that account for inspecting effects across the entire trial and improve the detection of event-related signal changes over common multiple comparisons correction strategies.
evidence: This is stated as a methodological feature in the abstract.

claim: The FLMM methodology improves the detection of event-related signal changes over common multiple comparisons correction strategies.
source: By exploiting signal autocorrelation, our methodology yields joint 95% confidence intervals that account for inspecting effects across the entire trial and improve the detection of event-related signal changes over common multiple comparisons correction strategies.
evidence: This is stated as a comparative advantage in the abstract.

claim: The FLMM framework revealed significant effects obscured by standard analysis approaches in a reanalysis of data from Jeong et al., 2022.
source: We reanalyze data from a recent study proposing a theory for the role of mesolimbic dopamine in reward learning, and show the capability of our framework to reveal significant effects obscured by standard analysis approaches.
evidence: This is stated as a result of applying the method to real data in the abstract.

claim: The FLMM method identified two dopamine components with distinct temporal dynamics in response to reward delivery.
source: For example, our method identifies two dopamine components with distinct temporal dynamics in response to reward delivery.
evidence: This is stated as a specific finding from the reanalysis in the abstract.

claim: In simulation experiments, the FLMM methodology yields improved statistical power over common analysis approaches.
source: In simulation experiments, our methodology yields improved statistical power over common analysis approaches.
evidence: This is stated as a result from simulation studies in the abstract.

claim: Fiber photometry quantifies bulk fluorescence emitted from fluorescent biosensors that detect neurotransmitters or physiological processes with high neurochemical and cell-type specificity.
source: The assay quantifies bulk fluorescence emitted from fluorescent biosensors that detect neurotransmitters or physiological processes (e.g. calcium influx) with high neurochemical and cell-type specificity (Cui et al., 2013; Gunaydin et al., 2014; Simpson et al., 2024).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations in the Introduction.

claim: The popularity of photometry has increased nearly exponentially since its development.
source: The popularity of photometry has increased nearly exponentially since its development (Cui et al., 2013; Gunaydin et al., 2014), with roughly 1500 references to it in the last year alone (see Appendix 1—figure 1 for an analysis of the number of references to photometry).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations and reference to an appendix figure in the Introduction.

claim: There is little consensus on analysis strategies for photometry data.
source: Although photometry is an invaluable tool, there is little consensus on analysis strategies for the data produced.
evidence: This is stated as a characterization of the field in the Introduction.

claim: Many common photometry analysis procedures grew organically out of adapting approaches historically applied in the cyclic voltammetry, EEG, and electrophysiology communities.
source: Many common analysis procedures were not designed for photometry, specifically, but rather grew organically out of adapting approaches historically applied in the cyclic voltammetry (Phillips et al., 2003; Heien et al., 2005), EEG (Adrian and Matthews, 1934), and electrophysiology communities (Fatt and Katz, 1952).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations in the Introduction.

claim: The most common photometry analysis strategy proceeds by averaging event-aligned signals across trials and animals, graphing each condition's average signal, calculating a signal summary measure, and conducting hypothesis tests on that summary statistic.
source: Arguably the most common photometry analysis strategy proceeds by: (1) averaging event-aligned signals across trials ('trial-averaging') and animals for comparison of different conditions (e.g. treatment/control), (2) graphing each condition's average signal ('trace'), (3) calculating a signal summary measure (e.g. Area Under the Curve [AUC]), and (4) conducting hypothesis tests (e.g. ANOVA) on that summary statistic.
evidence: This is stated as a characterization of common practice in the Introduction.

claim: Common photometry analysis conventions may dilute important patterns in the data related to individual animal differences in the timing and magnitude of signals, and the evolution of signals across trials.
source: Although these analysis conventions are parsimonious, they may dilute important patterns in the data related to, for example, individual animal differences in the timing and magnitude of signals, and the evolution of signals across trials.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of common approaches in the Introduction.

claim: Photometry can be applied in sophisticated multi-session longitudinal experiments because probes can be implanted chronically.
source: Part of the appeal of photometry is that probes can be implanted chronically, thereby enabling its application in sophisticated multi-session ('longitudinal') experiments.
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of photometry in the Introduction.

claim: Photometry signals exhibit considerable heterogeneity across animals.
source: Figure 1A shows that the signals exhibit considerable heterogeneity across animals, suggesting that it can be difficult to identify one summary measure that captures the target effect in all subjects.
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 1A showing data from Coddington et al., 2023.

claim: Photometry traces are highly variable across conditions within-animal.
source: Even within-animal, traces are highly variable across conditions (Figure 1B), trials within-session (Figure 1C), and sessions (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 1B showing data from Coddington et al., 2023.

claim: Photometry traces are highly variable across trials within-session.
source: Even within-animal, traces are highly variable across conditions (Figure 1B), trials within-session (Figure 1C), and sessions (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 1C showing data from Coddington et al., 2023.

claim: Photometry traces are highly variable across sessions.
source: Even within-animal, traces are highly variable across conditions (Figure 1B), trials within-session (Figure 1C), and sessions (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 1D showing data from Coddington et al., 2023.

claim: Averaging the signal across trials can obscure behavior–signal associations.
source: These figures illustrate how averaging the signal across trials can obscure behavior–signal associations, and how summarizing within trial signals (e.g. with AUC) can reduce one's ability to distinguish between trial-level signals that differ in dynamics, but yield similar summary values.
evidence: This is stated as an inference from the figures in the Introduction.

claim: Summarizing within trial signals with AUC can reduce one's ability to distinguish between trial-level signals that differ in dynamics but yield similar summary values.
source: These figures illustrate how averaging the signal across trials can obscure behavior–signal associations, and how summarizing within trial signals (e.g. with AUC) can reduce one's ability to distinguish between trial-level signals that differ in dynamics, but yield similar summary values.
evidence: This is stated as an inference from the figures in the Introduction.

claim: There are few analysis methods developed specifically for photometry.
source: Despite the complexity of the data, there are few analysis methods developed specifically for photometry.
evidence: This is stated as a characterization of the field in the Introduction.

claim: Encoding models of point-by-point signal-behavior relationships have been used for predicting signal values from behavioral variables.
source: Encoding models of point-by-point signal-behavior relationships have been used for predicting the signal values from behavioral variables (Markowitz et al., 2023; Willmore et al., 2022; Choi et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations in the Introduction.

claim: When encoding models are used for inference, they only test whether or not there is an overall behavioral effect on the signal in the analyzed time-window.
source: When used for inference, however, these approaches only test whether or not there is an overall behavioral effect on the signal in the analyzed time-window.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of encoding models in the Introduction.

claim: Encoding models do not test the association at each time-point, making it difficult to determine when the temporal dynamics of associations are meaningful.
source: By not testing the association at each time-point, it makes it difficult to determine when the temporal dynamics of associations are meaningful.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of encoding models in the Introduction.

claim: In encoding models, one model is fit per animal and thus data is not pooled across subjects, which can substantially reduce statistical power.
source: Moreover, one model is fit per animal and thus data is not pooled across subjects, which can substantially reduce statistical power.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of encoding models in the Introduction.

claim: Jean-Richard-Dit-Bressel et al., 2020 proposed to compare photometry signals through the combination of permutation testing and non-parametric bootstraps to construct confidence intervals.
source: In Jean-Richard-Dit-Bressel et al., 2020, the authors propose to compare photometry signals through the combination of permutation testing and non-parametric (cluster/subject-level) bootstraps to construct confidence intervals (CIs).
evidence: This is stated with a citation in the Introduction.

claim: The method proposed by Jean-Richard-Dit-Bressel et al., 2020 is restricted to comparisons between two conditions.
source: This is restricted to comparisons between two conditions, however, which precludes testing for continuous variables, multi-level factors, or multivariate analyses.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of the Jean-Richard-Dit-Bressel et al., 2020 method in the Introduction.

claim: Investigators have analyzed photometry and calcium imaging data by fitting pointwise generalized linear models or Pearson correlations to assess associations between variables and the signal at each trial time-point.
source: Investigators have analyzed data from techniques like photometry and calcium imaging by fitting pointwise generalized linear models (GLMs) (Pinto and Dan, 2015), or Pearson correlations (Markowitz et al., 2023) to assess associations between variables and the signal at each trial time-point.
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations in the Introduction.

claim: Standard GLMs and Pearson correlations do not yield valid inference when applied to multi-animal repeated measures datasets.
source: However, standard GLMs and Pearson correlations do not yield valid inference when applied to multi-animal repeated measures datasets.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of standard GLMs and correlations in the Introduction.

claim: Standard GLMs and Pearson correlations require one to analyze a single trial-averaged signal per animal, discarding trial-level information.
source: This, therefore, requires one to analyze a single trial-averaged signal per animal, discarding trial-level information.
evidence: This is stated as a consequence of the limitation of standard GLMs and correlations in the Introduction.

claim: Standard GLMs and Pearson correlations do not adjust for multiple comparisons of testing at different time-points, which can inflate Type I errors.
source: Moreover, the methods do not adjust for multiple comparisons of testing at different time-points, which can inflate Type I errors.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of standard GLMs and correlations in the Introduction.

claim: Lee et al., 2019 fit pointwise linear mixed models and then apply Benjamini-Hochberg correction.
source: Lee et al., 2019 fit pointwise linear mixed models and then apply Benjamini-Hochberg correction.
evidence: This is stated with a citation in the Introduction.

claim: The method by Lee et al., 2019 does not yield joint CIs and thus does not exploit the correlation between signal values across time-points.
source: However, this method does not yield joint CIs and thus does not exploit the correlation between signal values across time-points.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of the Lee et al., 2019 method in the Introduction.

claim: The method by Lee et al., 2019 requires one to adjust for a different test at each sample in a trial's signal.
source: The method, therefore, requires one to adjust for a different test at each sample in a trial's signal.
evidence: This is stated as a consequence of the Lee et al., 2019 method in the Introduction.

claim: Two analyses of the same data using the Lee et al., 2019 method, down-sampled with different sampling rates, could yield significant results in one analysis and not the other.
source: Thus, two analyses of the same data, down-sampled with different sampling rates, could yield significant results in one analysis and not the other, simply because higher sampling rates require one to correct for more comparisons.
evidence: This is stated as a consequence of the Lee et al., 2019 method in the Introduction.

claim: The Lee et al., 2019 method can be very conservative and dramatically hinder the detection of effects.
source: More generally, this method can be very conservative and dramatically hinder the detection of effects.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of the Lee et al., 2019 method in the Introduction.

claim: Existing photometry analysis approaches reduce the ability to detect effects.
source: In sum, we argue that existing photometry analysis approaches reduce the ability to detect effects.
evidence: This is stated as a summary of limitations in the Introduction.

claim: Summary measure analyses coarsen information by condensing the photometry signal into a single statistic that summarizes across time-points within-trial.
source: Summary measure analyses coarsen information by (1) condensing the photometry signal into a single statistic (e.g. AUC) that summarizes across time-points within-trial, and/or (2) averaging across-trials for each animal before conducting hypothesis tests.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of summary measure analyses in the Introduction.

claim: Summary measure analyses coarsen information by averaging across-trials for each animal before conducting hypothesis tests.
source: Summary measure analyses coarsen information by (1) condensing the photometry signal into a single statistic (e.g. AUC) that summarizes across time-points within-trial, and/or (2) averaging across-trials for each animal before conducting hypothesis tests.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of summary measure analyses in the Introduction.

claim: Methods that estimate associations at each trial time-point can obscure effects because current approaches do not exploit the correlation across time-points.
source: For methods that estimate associations at each trial time-point, effects can be obscured because current approaches do not exploit the correlation across time-points, do not provide joint CIs, and thus yield very conservative inference.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of existing time-point methods in the Introduction.

claim: Methods that estimate associations at each trial time-point do not provide joint CIs and thus yield very conservative inference.
source: For methods that estimate associations at each trial time-point, effects can be obscured because current approaches do not exploit the correlation across time-points, do not provide joint CIs, and thus yield very conservative inference.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of existing time-point methods in the Introduction.

claim: The proposed FLMM approach is based on functional linear mixed models.
source: We present an analysis framework that fills this gap and extracts more nuanced information from photometry data by (1) enabling hypothesis testing of the effects of experimental variables on signals at every trial time-point, and (2) using the signal from every trial and animal in the analysis. Our proposed approach is based on functional linear mixed models and allows one to compare the temporal evolution ('temporal dynamics') of the signal between conditions – in timing and magnitude – while accounting for between-animal differences.
evidence: This is stated as a description of the proposed method in the Introduction.

claim: The proposed FLMM approach allows one to compare the temporal evolution of the signal between conditions in timing and magnitude while accounting for between-animal differences.
source: Our proposed approach is based on functional linear mixed models and allows one to compare the temporal evolution ('temporal dynamics') of the signal between conditions – in timing and magnitude – while accounting for between-animal differences.
evidence: This is stated as a capability of the proposed method in the Introduction.

claim: The FLMM statistical procedure uses mixed effects modeling to enable the analysis of sophisticated nested experiments.
source: The statistical procedure uses (1) mixed effects modeling to enable the analysis of sophisticated nested experiments (e.g. designs that include multiple conditions, sessions, and trials), and (2) functional regression to exploit autocorrelation in the signal to calculate joint 95% CIs.
evidence: This is stated as a component of the proposed method in the Introduction.

claim: The FLMM statistical procedure uses functional regression to exploit autocorrelation in the signal to calculate joint 95% CIs.
source: The statistical procedure uses (1) mixed effects modeling to enable the analysis of sophisticated nested experiments (e.g. designs that include multiple conditions, sessions, and trials), and (2) functional regression to exploit autocorrelation in the signal to calculate joint 95% CIs.
evidence: This is stated as a component of the proposed method in the Introduction.

claim: The FLMM joint 95% CIs account for examining effects throughout the entire trial but are not overly conservative.
source: These joint CIs account for examining effects throughout the entire trial, but are not overly conservative CIs.
evidence: This is stated as a property of the proposed method in the Introduction.

claim: The FLMM framework outputs a plot for each covariate in the model which shows whether that covariate is significantly associated with the photometry signal at each time-point.
source: Our framework outputs a plot for each covariate in the model (e.g. behavior, cue-type), which shows whether that covariate is significantly associated with the photometry signal at each time-point.
evidence: This is stated as an output of the proposed method in the Introduction.

claim: The FLMM framework unifies the stages of plotting signals and then conducting hypothesis tests into a joint analysis and visualization procedure.
source: The framework, therefore, unifies the stages of plotting signals and then conducting hypothesis tests into a joint analysis and visualization procedure.
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of the proposed method in the Introduction.

claim: Linear mixed models are a class of methods for testing the association between covariates and outcomes for repeated measures data.
source: Linear mixed models (LMM) are a class of methods for testing the association between covariates ('independent' variables) and outcomes ('dependent' variables) for repeated measures data (see Methods section Linear mixed models for a brief introduction to LMM).
evidence: This is stated as a definition in the Results section.

claim: LMM can be used to analyze trial-level summary measures pooled across all trials and animals, preventing the loss of information from trial-averaging.
source: They can be used to analyze trial-level summary measures (e.g. AUCs) pooled across all trials and animals, preventing the loss of information from trial-averaging.
evidence: This is stated as a capability of LMM in the Results section.

claim: LMM still requires condensing signals into scalar summary measures, which coarsens within-trial information across time-points.
source: However, this still requires condensing signals into scalar summary measures, which coarsens within-trial information across time-points.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of LMM in the Results section.

claim: Functional regression methods can be used to model a photometry time series as a 'function', making it possible to test the association between covariates of interest and the signal value at each time-point in the trial.
source: In contrast, functional regression methods can be used to model a photometry time series as a 'function,' which makes it possible to test the association between covariates of interest and the signal value at each time-point in the trial (see Methods section Functional linear regression for a brief introduction to functional regression).
evidence: This is stated as a capability of functional regression in the Results section.

claim: Most functional regression methods require trial averaging of the signals prior to analysis, which discards trial-level information.
source: However, most functional regression methods require trial averaging of the signals prior to analysis, which discards trial-level information.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of functional regression in the Results section.

claim: FLMM combines the benefits of LMM and functional regression to extract the information in the signal both across- and within- trials.
source: The photometry analysis framework we are introducing is based on Functional Linear Mixed Models (FLMM), which combines the benefits of LMM and functional regression to extract the information in the signal both across- and within- trials (Cui et al., 2022; Scheipl et al., 2015; Davidson, 2009; Morris and Carroll, 2006).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations in the Results section.

claim: FLMM estimates the effects and statistical significance of covariates that can vary between trial, session, and animal for longitudinal designs.
source: By modeling covariates that can vary between (1) trial (e.g. cue-type, latency-to-press), (2) session (e.g. training stage), and (3) animal (e.g. treatment group), FLMM estimates the effects (termed functional fixed-effects) and statistical significance of those covariates for longitudinal designs.
evidence: This is stated as a capability of FLMM in the Results section.

claim: FLMM can estimate and adjust for between-animal differences in photometry signal dynamics and effects of a covariate on the signal within- and across- trials through functional random-effects.
source: By further including functional random-effects, the framework can also estimate and adjust for between-animal differences in (1) photometry signal dynamics, and (2) effects of a covariate on the signal, within- and across- trials.
evidence: This is stated as a capability of FLMM in the Results section.

claim: FLMM enables one to model between-animal and between-trial variability in both the 'shape' of the signal and the evolution of covariate effects across trial time-points.
source: In essence, this enables one to model between-animal and between-trial variability in both the 'shape' of the signal, and the evolution of covariate effects across trial time-points.
evidence: This is stated as a capability of FLMM in the Results section.

claim: The FLMM result is a single plot of the coefficient estimates for each covariate, which visualizes when and to what extent the covariate has a statistically significant association with the photometry signal during a trial.
source: The result is a single plot of the coefficient estimates for each covariate, which visualizes when (and to what extent) the covariate has a statistically significant (fixed-effect) association with the photometry signal during a trial.
evidence: This is stated as an output of FLMM in the Results section.

claim: FLMM models each trial's signal as a function that varies smoothly across trial time-points.
source: FLMM models each trial's signal as a function that varies smoothly across trial time-points (i.e. along the 'functional domain').
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of FLMM in the Results section.

claim: FLMM is a type of non-linear modeling technique over the functional domain.
source: It is thus a type of non-linear modeling technique over the functional domain, since we do not assume a linear model (straight line).
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of FLMM in the Results section.

claim: FLMM and other functional data analysis methods model data as functions when there is a natural ordering and are assumed to vary smoothly along the functional domain.
source: FLMM and other functional data analysis methods model data as functions, when there is a natural ordering (e.g. time-series data are ordered by time, imaging data are ordered by x-y coordinates), and are assumed to vary smoothly along the functional domain (e.g. one assumes values of a photometry signal at close time-points in a trial have similar values).
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of functional data analysis methods in the Results section.

claim: Functional data analysis approaches exploit smoothness and natural ordering to capture additional information during estimation and inference.
source: Functional data analysis approaches exploit this smoothness and natural ordering to capture additional information during estimation and inference.
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of functional data analysis methods in the Results section.

claim: The FLMM approach is based on an estimation procedure first proposed in Cui et al., 2022.
source: Our FLMM approach is based on an estimation procedure that was first proposed in Cui et al., 2022.
evidence: This is stated with a citation in the Results section.

claim: The Cui et al., 2022 method was selected because it allows for calculation of joint 95% CIs, is readily scalable for neuroscience experiments, and uses common syntax from the lme4 package.
source: We selected this method because (1) it allows for calculation of joint 95% CIs, (2) it is readily scalable for the dataset sizes and random-effect specifications needed for neuroscience experiments, and (3) it uses common syntax for model specification from the well-known lme4 package.
evidence: This is stated as justification for method selection in the Results section.

claim: Joint CIs in FLMM take into account the autocorrelation of signal values across trial time-points.
source: Compared with pointwise CIs, joint CIs take into account the autocorrelation of signal values across trial time-points (the functional domain).
evidence: This is stated as a property of joint CIs in the Results section.

claim: Joint CIs enable joint interpretations at multiple locations along the functional domain instead of at a specific time-point.
source: Therefore, instead of interpreting results at a specific time-point, joint CIs enable joint interpretations at multiple locations along the functional domain.
evidence: This is stated as a property of joint CIs in the Results section.

claim: Joint CIs align with interpreting covariate effects on photometry signals across time-intervals as opposed to at a single trial time-point.
source: This aligns with interpreting covariate effects on the photometry signals across time-intervals (e.g. a cue period) as opposed to at a single trial time-point.
evidence: This is stated as a property of joint CIs in the Results section.

claim: Previous methodological work has provided functional mixed model implementations for either joint 95% CIs for simple random-effects models or pointwise 95% CIs for nested models, but not joint 95% CIs for general random-effects specifications.
source: Previous methodological work has provided functional mixed model implementations for either joint 95% CIs for simple random-effects models (Cui et al., 2022), or pointwise 95% CIs for nested models (Scheipl et al., 2016), but to our knowledge, do not provide explicit formulas or software for computing joint 95% CIs in the presence of general random-effects specifications.
evidence: This is stated with citations as a gap in existing methods in the Results section.

claim: Nested random-effects specifications substantially improved model fits in the neuroscience experiments reanalyzed.
source: We found nested random-effects specifications substantially improved model fits in the neuroscience experiments we reanalyzed, and helped model sophisticated behavioral designs (see Appendix 3.3 for more details).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the reanalyses in the Results section.

claim: The authors derived an extension of the estimator for the covariance of the random-effects based on a Method of Moments approach described by Greven et al., 2010.
source: We, therefore, derived an extension of the estimator for the covariance of the random-effects (Cui et al., 2022), based on a Method of Moments approach described by Greven et al., 2010.
evidence: This is stated with citations as a methodological contribution in the Results section.

claim: Each period for which the joint 95% CI does not contain 0 anywhere denotes that the fixed-effect coefficients are statistically significantly different from 0 throughout the entire period.
source: Each period for which the joint 95% CI does not contain 0 anywhere denotes that the fixed-effect coefficients are statistically significantly different from 0 throughout the entire period.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of FLMM output in the Results section.

claim: The FLMM plot conveys where effects are statistically significant, the estimated effect magnitudes, and joint 95% CIs.
source: The plot conveys: (1) where effects are statistically significant; (2) the estimated effect magnitudes; and (3) joint 95% CIs, thereby providing a complete, interpretable, and simplified presentation of statistical results.
evidence: This is stated as a description of FLMM output in the Results section.

claim: The dataset from Jeong et al., 2022 exhibits many common characteristics of photometry data that can dilute effects or invalidate results if left unaccounted for.
source: We used this study for two reasons. First, the dataset exhibits many common characteristics of photometry data that can dilute effects, or even invalidate results if left unaccounted for.
evidence: This is stated as justification for dataset selection in the Results section.

claim: The dataset from Jeong et al., 2022 contains data from multiple experiments, allowing illustration of how FLMM can be used to test hypotheses across a range of experimental designs.
source: Second, the dataset contains data from multiple experiments, which allows us to illustrate how FLMM can be used to test hypotheses across a range of experimental designs.
evidence: This is stated as justification for dataset selection in the Results section.

claim: The dopamine measurements in Jeong et al., 2022 were collected in within-subject nested longitudinal experiments.
source: One of the most important characteristics of these data is that the dopamine (DA) measurements were collected in within-subject nested longitudinal experiments.
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of the dataset in the Results section.

claim: Photometry experiments often exhibit nested longitudinal structure, which can induce correlation patterns in the data within-animal and obscure effects if not accounted for statistically.
source: Photometry experiments often exhibit this type of nested longitudinal structure, which can induce correlation patterns in the data within-animal, and obscure effects if not accounted for statistically.
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of photometry experiments in the Results section.

claim: The Jeong et al., 2022 data exhibited high within-animal correlations across sessions.
source: For example, these data exhibited high within-animal correlations across sessions (Figure 3E), and across trials within-session (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 3E in the Results section.

claim: The Jeong et al., 2022 data exhibited high within-animal correlations across trials within-session.
source: For example, these data exhibited high within-animal correlations across sessions (Figure 3E), and across trials within-session (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 3F in the Results section.

claim: FLMM can model effect heterogeneity and correlation patterns within- and across- trials through the inclusion of functional random-effects.
source: FLMM can model effect heterogeneity, as well as correlation patterns within- and across- trials, through the inclusion of functional random-effects.
evidence: This is stated as a capability of FLMM in the Results section.

claim: Functional random-effects in FLMM allow one to estimate what is common across all animals and what is unique to each.
source: These allow one to estimate what is common across all animals, and what is unique to each.
evidence: This is stated as a capability of functional random-effects in the Results section.

claim: Photometry datasets often exhibit between-animal variability in covariate-signal associations.
source: This is critical because photometry datasets often exhibit between-animal variability in covariate-signal associations.
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of photometry data in the Results section.

claim: In the Jeong et al., 2022 random IRI task, the magnitude of the IRI-AUC correlation varied considerably across animals and sessions.
source: Figure 3G shows that the magnitude of this correlation varied considerably across animals and sessions.
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 3G in the Results section.

claim: FLMM can model variability in IRI–DA correlation magnitude through the inclusion of animal- and session-specific random effects.
source: FLMM can model this variability in IRI–DA correlation magnitude through the inclusion of animal- and session-specific random effects.
evidence: This is stated as a capability of FLMM in the Results section.

claim: By varying which covariates and random-effects are included in the model, FLMM can analyze data from experimental designs that include within- and between-subject contrasts.
source: More broadly, by varying which covariates and random-effects are included in the model, FLMM can analyze data from experimental designs that include within- and between-subject contrasts.
evidence: This is stated as a capability of FLMM in the Results section.

claim: FLMM can accommodate missing data and subjects with different sample sizes.
source: Finally, FLMM can accommodate missing data and subjects with different sample sizes, which are often unavoidable characteristics of photometry experiments.
evidence: This is stated as a capability of FLMM in the Results section.

claim: The Jeong et al., 2022 dataset included photometry recordings of behavioral sessions at various stages of training that differed across animals.
source: In Figure 3H we show how this dataset included photometry recordings of behavioral sessions at various stages of training that differed across animals.
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 3H in the Results section.

claim: FLMM can help model signal components unrelated to the scientific question of interest and provides a systematic framework to quantify the additional uncertainty from those modeling choices.
source: FLMM can help model signal components unrelated to the scientific question of interest, and provides a systematic framework to quantify the additional uncertainty from those modeling choices.
evidence: This is stated as a capability of FLMM in the Discussion.

claim: Analysts sometimes normalize data with trial-specific baselines because longitudinal experiments can induce correlation patterns across trials that standard techniques may not adequately account for.
source: For example, analysts sometimes normalize data with trial-specific baselines because longitudinal experiments can induce correlation patterns across trials that standard techniques (e.g. repeated measures ANOVA) may not adequately account for.
evidence: This is stated as a rationale for a common practice in the Discussion.

claim: Even without many standard data pre-processing steps, FLMM provides smooth estimation results across trial time-points, has the ability to adjust for between-trial and -animal heterogeneity, and provides a valid statistical inference approach that quantifies the resulting uncertainty.
source: Even without many standard data pre-processing steps, FLMM provides smooth estimation results across trial time-points (the 'functional domain'), has the ability to adjust for between-trial and -animal heterogeneity, and provides a valid statistical inference approach that quantifies the resulting uncertainty.
evidence: This is stated as a capability of FLMM in the Discussion.

claim: Session-to-session variability in signal magnitudes or dynamics could be accounted for through the inclusion of trial-level fixed or random effects in FLMM.
source: For instance, session-to-session variability in signal magnitudes or dynamics (e.g. a decreasing baseline within-session from bleaching or satiation) could be accounted for, at least in part, through the inclusion of trial-level fixed or random effects.
evidence: This is stated as a capability of FLMM in the Discussion.

claim: Signal heterogeneity due to subject characteristics could be incorporated into an FLMM model through the inclusion of animal-specific random effects.
source: Similarly, signal heterogeneity due to subject characteristics (e.g. sex, CS+ cue identity) could be incorporated into a model through the inclusion of animal-specific random effects.
evidence: This is stated as a capability of FLMM in the Discussion.

claim: Inclusion of fixed or random effects in FLMM would influence the width of the confidence intervals.
source: Inclusion of these effects would then influence the width of the confidence intervals.
evidence: This is stated as a consequence of model specification in the Discussion.

claim: By expressing one's 'beliefs' in an FLMM model specification, one can compare models with AIC.
source: By expressing one's 'beliefs' in an FLMM model specification, one can compare models (e.g. with AIC).
evidence: This is stated as a capability of FLMM in the Discussion.

claim: The level of smoothing in FLMM is largely selected as a function of the data and is accounted for directly in the equations used to construct confidence intervals.
source: Even the level of smoothing in FLMM is largely selected as a function of the data, and is accounted for directly in the equations used to construct confidence intervals.
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of FLMM in the Discussion.

claim: FLMM is applicable in a wide range of experimental settings.
source: FLMM is applicable in a wide range of experimental settings.
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of FLMM in the Discussion.

claim: The authors provide an analysis guide and open source package, fastFMM, that is the first to provide joint CIs for functional mixed models with nested random-effects.
source: We provide an analysis guide and open source package, fastFMM (our package is available on CRAN and also at https://github.com/gloewing/fastFMM, which has links to our analysis guide and examples of using the package in both R and python), that is the first, to our knowledge, to provide joint CIs for functional mixed models with nested random-effects.
evidence: This is stated as a contribution in the Discussion.

claim: The authors selected a dataset collected on a behavioral paradigm, photometry sensor, and signaling pathway that are well characterized, making it easier to evaluate the framework.
source: For demonstration, we selected a dataset collected on a behavioral paradigm, photometry sensor, and signaling pathway that are well characterized, making it easier to evaluate the framework.

claim: Selecting summary measures and time-windows to quantify is relatively easy in the Jeong et al., 2022 dataset, but may not be the case when collecting data under new conditions.
source: Although selecting summary measures and time-windows to quantify is relatively easy here, this may not be the case when collecting data under new conditions.

claim: FLMM can characterize the association between neural activity and covariates without strong assumptions about how to summarize signals.
source: In such cases, FLMM can characterize the association between neural activity and covariates without strong assumptions about how to summarize signals.
evidence: This is stated as a capability of FLMM in the Discussion.

claim: The fastFMM package is fast and maintains a low memory footprint even for complex models and relatively large datasets.
source: Importantly, the package is fast and maintains a low memory footprint even for complex models and relatively large datasets (see Functional mixed models package for an example).

claim: The FLMM framework may also be applicable to techniques like electrophysiology and calcium imaging.
source: The FLMM framework may also be applicable to techniques like electrophysiology and calcium imaging.

claim: The fastFMM package can fit functional generalized LMMs with a count distribution.
source: For example, our package can fit functional generalized LMMs with a count distribution (e.g. Poisson).

claim: The FLMM method can be extended to model time-varying covariates.
source: Additionally, our method can be extended to model time-varying covariates.

source: This would enable one to estimate how the level of association between signals, simultaneously recorded from different brain regions, fluctuates across trial time-points.

claim: Extending FLMM to model time-varying covariates would enable modeling of trials that differ in length due to variable behavioral response times.
source: This would also enable modeling of trials that differ in length due to, for example, variable behavioral response times (e.g. latency-to-press).
evidence: This is stated as a potential application of an extension in the Discussion.

claim: The authors specified FLMM models with linear covariate–signal relationships at a fixed trial time-point across trials/sessions to compare the FLMM analogue of the analyses conducted in Jeong et al., 2022.
source: In this paper, we specified FLMM models with linear covariate–signal relationships at a fixed trial time-point across trials/sessions, to compare the FLMM analogue of the analyses conducted in Jeong et al., 2022.
evidence: This is stated as a description of the modeling approach in the Discussion.

claim: The fastFMM package allows the modeling of covariate–signal relationships with non-linear functions of covariates, using splines or other basis functions.
source: However, our package allows the modeling of covariate–signal relationships with non-linear functions of covariates, using splines or other basis functions.

claim: One must consider the tradeoff between flexibility and interpretability when specifying potentially complex FLMM models, especially since FLMM is designed for statistical inference.
source: One must consider, however, the tradeoff between flexibility and interpretability when specifying potentially complex models, especially since FLMM is designed for statistical inference.

claim: Research on statistical methods for fiber photometry is necessary, given the widespread use of the technique and the variability of analysis procedures across labs.
source: To conclude, we believe research on statistical methods for fiber photometry is necessary, given the widespread use of the technique and the variability of analysis procedures across labs.
